checks.name: published map has no direct NULL replacement
published map has no direct deallocation
initial namespace uses positive PID maximum
callsite invokes allocator only in function once
generic SMP API routes store release
generic SMP API routes load acquire
x86 release is compiler barrier then WRITE_ONCE
x86 acquire is READ_ONCE then compiler barrier

model_abstraction.consumer_guard: The payload read executes only after the publication read returns nonzero.
model_abstraction.omitted: Allocation internals, array contents and unrelated tracing state cannot affect the selected two-location ordering property.
model_abstraction.tgid_map: 0 is NULL and 1 is the single successfully allocated non-NULL pointer.
model_abstraction.tgid_map_max: 0 is static pre-initialization state and 1 is the positive assigned value.

property.claim: On the configured SMP x86-64 profile, if trace_find_tgid_ptr() observes the non-NULL tgid_map value published by a successful trace_alloc_tgid_map(), its following tgid_map_max access cannot observe the pre-publication zero value.

compiler_architecture_argument.architecture_mapping: The accepted scope relies on the Linux x86-64 implementation satisfying LKMM release/acquire semantics; the object inspection confirms this selected build but is not a proof of the x86 ISA or arbitrary compiler versions.
compiler_architecture_argument.compiler_mapping: The pinned x86 macros place compiler barriers around volatile WRITE_ONCE/READ_ONCE operations, and the configured object preserves payload-before-publication and publication-before-payload-read instruction order.
compiler_architecture_argument.kernel_contract: The pinned memory-barriers documentation guarantees that accesses before a release become visible after an acquire that reads the same published value.

exclusions: No tgid_map element contents, pid bounds, allocation arithmetic, tracing API behavior or whole-function memory safety is verified.
No architecture other than the configured SMP x86-64 profile is accepted by this pilot.
The model does not establish progress, fairness, allocation success, lock freedom or wait freedom.
Future pointer replacement or reclamation would invalidate the retained lifetime argument and must fail source identities.
The model checks one successful publisher and one reader; it is not a whole tracing-subsystem concurrency proof.

lifetime.allocation: The published pointer comes from a successful kvzalloc_objs() call.
lifetime.reclamation: The translation unit contains no later NULL assignment or deallocation of tgid_map.
lifetime.scope: Only the max-publication ordering before any hypothetical future source change that adds replacement or reclamation.
lifetime.storage: Both publication variables are translation-unit-local static objects.

producer_serialization.argument: The sole callsite is the RECORD_TGID arm of set_tracer_flag(), whose matching arm asserts event_mutex ownership. The allocator returns immediately after publication on later calls.

consumer_observe.argument: The model observes the same publication variable and represents NULL/non-NULL by 0/1.

consumer_payload.argument: C short-circuiting reads tgid_map_max only when map is non-NULL. The model preserves that guard and asks only whether this read can see old zero.

producer_payload.argument: Both objects have static zero initialization. PID_MAX_DEFAULT is positive; the model value 1 distinguishes the assigned maximum from its old zero value without depending on its magnitude.

producer_publish.argument: The condition selects only a successful allocation and abstracts its non-NULL pointer as 1.
